samples.summary: set-state.mjs's changed CI read (scoped endpoint + ciConclusion normalisation) has no behavioural test — only a source-regex pin
samples.evidence: `gatherSignals` was changed from "fetch every run for the SHA, filter by display name 'CI', newest by created_at" to "fetch /actions/workflows/ci.yml/runs and normalise via ciConclusion" (set-state.mjs:226-234). The only thing that exercises this change is a text assertion in checks.test.mjs:732-744 (`assert.match(src, /actions\/workflows\/\$\{CI_WORKFLOW_FILE\}\/runs\?head_sha=/)`), i.e. it checks the URL literal in the source, not the behaviour. set-state.test.mjs imports only the pure helpers (STATES, labelFor, computeLabelSet, deriveState — lines 3-12) and there is no gh-stub process harness for set-state as there is for mark-ready, so the new semantics (a newest in-flight run now yields null; 'cancelled'/'timed_out' now yield 'failure'; ordering by id rather than created_at) are never observed end-to-end. Impact is contained (a wrong agent:* lifecycle label / a skipped reconcile), which is why this is minor rather than major.

samples.summary: The 1000-file boundary the test claims to guard is not covered — the comment says "exactly 1000 files is fine" while the assertion pins the opposite
samples.evidence: mark-ready.test.mjs:415-422 says "Exactly 1000 files is fine; 10 full pages is what the bound allows, and an off-by-one here would refuse a legal PR" and then asserts `atTheBound.code === 1` for ten full pages — i.e. it asserts that exactly-1000-files IS refused. The loop in mark-ready.mjs (`for (let page = 1; page <= 10; page++) { ... if (files.length < 100) return hits; } throw`) cannot distinguish 1000 from >1000 without an 11th request, so the documented "exactly 1000 is fine" behaviour does not exist and nothing tests it. A reader of this test believes the off-by-one is pinned when the only assertion is that the bound refuses; a future change that shifted the bound (e.g. `page <= 11`) would fail this test while the property the comment names remains untested.
searchedFor: Read mark-ready.test.mjs 'gate 1b enumerates EVERY page' test

samples.summary: Nothing pins `set +e` around the mark-ready invocation in the promote step, so removing it would silently turn "gates unsatisfied" into a red job with no test failure
samples.evidence: The promote step's whole exit-code branching depends on `set +e` before the invocation and `set -e` after (agent-review-panel.yml, diff hunk at the 'Run ready gate' step). mark-ready.test.mjs's consumer test (lines 667-778) asserts the invocation flags, the redirect, `code=$?`, the `case` labels and each branch's exits — but a grep for `set +e` across scripts/agent finds no assertion anywhere. Delete `set +e` and the step aborts at the invocation for exit 1 (a legitimately-unready PR), so the job reds and no `outcome` is ever recorded — the mis-attribution this change exists to remove — while every test stays green. Same for the newly added `cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/mark-ready.log" || true`: nothing asserts the report is echoed back or that the `|| true` protects the `case`.
searchedFor: Read mark-ready.test.mjs 'agent-review-panel.yml handles every mark-ready code' test in full

samples.summary: The path-parsing regression guard is spelling-specific: `!/split("@")/` only catches one literal, so an equivalent regressed reader passes
samples.evidence: checks.test.mjs:743 and :745 assert `!/split\("@"\)/.test(src)` for mark-ready.mjs, set-state.mjs and checks.mjs. The regression it claims to close (parsing an attacker-influenced run path) reappears unchanged if written as `split('@')`, `path.replace(/@.*/, '')`, `indexOf("@")`, or any JS-side `r.path === ...` match, none of which this guard sees. The behavioural test in mark-ready.test.mjs:267-320 does cover the unscoped-endpoint regression, so this is a weak belt over a covered property rather than the only coverage — but as written the assertion reads as a guard against a class of bug while pinning a single string.
searchedFor: Read checks.test.mjs 'the CI readers scope by workflow FILE' test

samples.summary: The 101-run "page-2 case" fixture cannot distinguish a paginated listing from a truncated one — pagination is only pinned by regex
samples.evidence: checks.test.mjs:786-789 adds a 101-element fixture described as "The page-2 case: 101 runs is impossible to reach through `per_page: 1`", but the fixture is only fed to the extracted selection function (`mirror(fixture)`, line 820), which receives the whole list directly and never performs the API listing. Whether the workflow actually paginates is pinned only by the text assertions at lines 807-809 (`github.paginate(...)`, `per_page: 100`). The test's own comment acknowledges this ("Not covered by extracting the selection below"), so this is honest, but the fixture contributes no coverage beyond the smaller ones and can read as pagination coverage that is not there.
searchedFor: Read checks.test.mjs 'agent-rerun / agent-loop mirror ciRunToRerun inline' test

samples.summary: Gate 1b's second head read (`gh pr view N --json headRefOid`) failing is untested, though the stub can express it
samples.evidence: mark-ready.test.mjs covers the moved-head case (`headAfter: "beef8"`, line 472) but not the case where the re-read itself throws; the stub's `fail` prefix list could express it as `fail: ["pr view 7 --json headRefOid"]`. The branch falls into `ranBaseCiDefinition`'s catch and refuses (exit 1), which is the desired fail-closed outcome, so the impact of a regression here is contained — but it is a distinct untested path in newly added evidence-pinning logic.
